name: Le Bristol Paris
address: 112 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, 75008 Paris, France
tagline: A hundred suites and a French garden on the rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré.
description:
Le Bristol Paris is a palace hotel at 112 rue du Faubourg Saint-Honoré, five minutes on foot from the Champs-Élysées. It has 188 rooms, 100 of them suites, a garden à la française, a three-Michelin-star restaurant and a swimming pool on the sixth floor.

The hotel opened in April 1925 on the former property of Jules de Castellane and takes its name from Frederick Hervey, 4th Earl of Bristol, an eighteenth-century traveller. The Oetker family acquired it in 1978, and in 2011 it became the first hotel in France to receive the Palace distinction. It stands among the fashion houses and galleries of the Faubourg.

Rooms begin at 35 square metres and suites at 55. Eleven signature suites sit at the top of the range: the Suite Impériale and the Suite Royale each cover 320 square metres, the Suite Paris and the Suite Honeymoon face the Eiffel Tower, and the Suite Panoramique looks toward Montmartre and the Opéra Garnier. The Suite Eden and the Suite Azur look over the garden. Each room is decorated differently, and the hotel still uses the original room keys rather than cards.

Epicure, led by Chef Arnaud Faye, has held three Michelin stars since 2009. It serves six- and eight-course tasting menus, has a dining terrace in the garden, and requires a jacket. Café Antonia, with frescoed walls and crystal chandeliers, serves from breakfast to dinner and afternoon tea. Le Jardin Français is a planted courtyard for lunch and drinks, and Le Bar du Bristol keeps a short list of signature cocktails. Les Ateliers du Bristol turn out bread from the hotel's own mill, chocolate, cheese and pasta in house.

Spa Le Bristol by La Mer has eight treatment rooms, two of them duo suites, and opens onto an interior garden. The indoor pool on the sixth floor was designed in the early 1980s by the naval architect Cäsar Pinnau in the manner of a 1920s yacht deck, with teak floors, a solarium facing Sacré-Cœur and windows toward the Eiffel Tower. The water is kept at 28 degrees and the pool is open daily from 6.30 am to 10.30 pm to hotel guests only. A fitness room has Pilates Reformer equipment.

The hotel suits travellers who want a Paris palace with its own garden and kitchens in the middle of the shopping and gallery district. Paris Orly is about 20 kilometres away and Charles de Gaulle 30, and the hotel arranges limousine transfers. Pets up to 7 kilograms are welcome.
